title: エルサルバドル、ハイチのギャングによる人質事件受け対応へ

sources.headline: El Salvador's president threatens Haitian gangs over military hostages
sources.text: El Salvador's president has said he has launched a military operation to rescue four air force personnel who have been missing in Haiti since Sunday. Threatening further action, Nayib Bukele said that Wednesday's attack was "nothing" compared with what would happen if all the hostages - who he said were not combatants - were not returned alive. They went missing after being ambushed by "heavily armed criminal groups," El Salvador's armed forces said. The ambush occurred in Croix-des-Bouquets, an area controlled by armed groups. They were part of the so-called Gang Suppression Force (GSF), approved by the United Nations Security Council earlier this month, to tackle escalating gang violence in Haiti. According to an X post from Bukele, the mission consisted of pilots and technical personnel, whose primary jobs were to "carry out medical evacuations and save lives, not to wage war". His post said the Salvadoran military operation's single objective was to bring the four men back home alive. He added that if all four were returned alive, without being harmed, "everything will go back to how it was before the kidnapping". Bukele added they were kidnapped "in a cowardly manner" while returning after buying food at a market in the area.A statement released by the Armed Forces of El Salvador on Sunday said the group was ambushed while travelling back to its camp in an armoured vehicle, which caught fire after being hit by explosives. So far, no gang has claimed responsibility for the attack.Salvadoran helicopters were deployed to assist, with multiple attempts to make an approach by land and air hampered by fighting and local security conditions, the armed forces said. On Wednesday, before Bukele announced the launch of the military operation, the GSF said it was searching for the four missing personnel following the attack. It added that it had "engaged armed gang elements, with helicopter support" and that early reports had indicated that several gang members were killed. Earlier this week, the UN warned that Haiti's armed gangs were adapting to intensified security conditions, saying that they were "stepping up reprisals against civilians and extending their reach into rural areas". Haiti has not held elections since 2016, and two weeks ago postponed presidential and legislative elections - scheduled for 13 December - indefinitely. The country has been wracked by economic chaos, a political vacuum and increasingly violent gang warfare since its president was assassinated in 2021.More than 5,500 people were killed in gang-related violence in Haiti in 2024. Armed gangs currently control about 85% of the capital, Port-au-Prince.

sources.headline: El Salvador’s President Issues Harsh Warning to Haitian Gangs After 4 Soldiers Are Abducted
Bukele says military operation launched to rescue Salvadorans held by gangs in Haiti
sources.text:
Armored police vehicles that are part of the Gang Suppression Force (GSF) patrol the Tabarre neighborhood of Port-au-Prince, Haiti, Monday, Oct. 19, 2026.
Odelyn Joseph/AP
hide caption
Odelyn Joseph/AP
SAN SALVADOR — El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele said Wednesday he had launched a military operation to rescue four Salvadoran aviation technicians kidnapped by gangs in Haiti, warning of a more forceful response if they are not released alive and unharmed.
Gangs in Haiti had opened fire on an armored vehicle three days earlier the first major attack since an international gang suppression force began operating in the violence-wracked Caribbean country. The four Salvadoran soldiers have been missing since they fled the burning vehicle in the Santo area of Croix-des-Bouquets, Port-au-Prince. Addressing Haitian gang leaders, Bukele demanded that they return the Salvadorans "alive, unharmed" and warned that, if they do so, "everything will go back to the way it was before the kidnapping." If not, the Salvadoran leader — who drew international attention for his contentious war on his own country's gangs — said it would result in a more powerful operation.
"Today's attack is nothing compared to what is coming if they do not release the four hostages alive. And do not take our words as empty threats," he wrote on the social media platform X. It was not immediately clear if Bukele intended any further action to be carried out by Salvadoran, Haitian or international security forces in the area. In his post, the Salvadoran leader shared video of armored vehicles with shattered windows driving through plumes of smoke. Haiti's government issued a news release Wednesday evening saying the "abduction" of the aviation technicians was an "absolute priority." It noted that a meeting was held at the prime minister's office "to assess the ongoing interventions and determine the necessary measures to strengthen operations, in close collaboration with the Gang Repression Force." "The release of the abducted soldiers is an absolute priority, and all necessary resources are being mobilized to achieve this goal," the government said. It wasn't immediately clear if Haitian authorities received confirmation that the Salvadoran soldiers are alive. A spokesperson for the gang suppression force did not immediately respond to a message seeking details. Bukele said the four men are aviation technicians and that the Salvadoran mission in Haiti "consists only of pilots and technical personnel" whose main job is to carry out medical evacuations, "not to wage war."
The U.N.-backed force is still fighting gangs in the community where Sunday's attack occurred, warning residents in the area to remain indoors. No one has claimed responsibility for the attack on the Salvadoran troops and it comes as Haiti prepares for its first general election in more than a decade. It also showcases the power of the gangs that control an estimated 70% of Port-au-Prince. El Salvador is among a number of countries – including Chad, Jamaica and Guatemala – to form a part of a gang suppression force with more than 2,000 troops on the ground in Haiti. The U.N. in 2025 originally approved up to 5,550 security personnel and more than 50 civilian staff to be sent to Haiti to dismantle armed gangs. In early October, El Salvador passed a law extending its armed forces' participation in the force for a year. The law also authorized the mission to "deploy civilian and military personnel according to the mission's needs," expanding its role beyond medical evacuations, as stipulated in the previous decree. The multinational force received at least a six-month extension through March 2027 from the U.N. Security Council. Gang violence has displaced nearly 1.5 million people in Haiti in recent years, with more than 5,700 people killed or injured from January through mid-September and more than 230 people kidnapped, according to the United Nations. The area where the armored vehicle was targeted is controlled by gangs including Chèn Méchan; Kraze Barye, led by Vitelhomme Innocent; and 400 Mawozo, led by Lanmo Sanjou. Both gang leaders have been sanctioned by the U.N. and the U.S.

sources.headline: El Salvador says Haiti gangs holding 4 force members hostage, announces new rescue mission
sources.text: Oct 21 - El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele on Wednesday said that Haitian gangs were holding four Salvadaron members of an international UN-backed security force hostage, and that he had launched a military operation to being them back unharmed.El Salvador's military and the Gang Suppression Force, mandated to help Haitian police fight powerful gangs, earlier this week announced efforts to recover the missing Salvadorans, but said intense fighting in the area had limited access.• "Today, we have launched a military operation to rescue them," Bukele said, without providing further details about the operation or identifying the group holding the Salvadorans hostage.• The Gang Suppression Force did not immediately respond to a request for comment.• The four Salvadorans went missing on Sunday after they leapt from a burning armored vehicle that was ambushed by armed gangs on the outskirts of the capital while returning from a market to their base, security officials said.• Haitian gangs have cemented their influence over the capital and expanded to surrounding regions over recent years off the back of a longstanding political vacuum, widespread extortion and a flow of illegal arms largely from the US.• Several nations including Chad and Sri Lanka have deployed soldiers as part of the Gang Suppression Force, which a year into its mandate has reached just over a third of its planned size and has had limited impact on Haiti's security.• Bukele said the missing men were aviation technicians, not combatants.• "Our mission consists only of pilots and technical personnel, whose primary job is to carry out medical evacuations and save lives, not to wage war," he said in a post X. REUTERS
